_doc: Per-analyte toxicology anchors + display metadata for the standards-page 'Occurrence & Derivation Rationale' section. Each `tox_anchor` is a faithful compression of the lead paragraph of the corresponding /analytes/<page> page (the published rationale surface), so the derivation prose stays grounded in — and consistent with — that page. `page` is the analyte-page slug for the one-way 'why it is limited' link. Hand-authored; re-check against content/analytes/<page>.md when a rationale page changes.

Pb.name: Lead
Pb.tox_anchor: lead's developmental neurotoxicity in young children has no demonstrated threshold, so the governing frame is to minimize exposure as far as practicable rather than to meet a safe dose

Cd.name: Cadmium
Cd.tox_anchor: cadmium is a cumulative nephrotoxicant with a renal half-life of 10 to 30 years and an IARC Group 1 carcinogen with no clinical treatment, so control is a matter of capping intake

iAs.name: Inorganic arsenic
iAs.tox_anchor: inorganic arsenic is an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen for which the assessment bodies have set no safe intake threshold, with dietary exposures already at or above the cancer reference point

tAs.name: Total arsenic
tAs.tox_anchor: total arsenic is regulated because its inorganic fraction is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen for which no safe intake threshold has been set

tHg.name: Total mercury
tHg.tox_anchor: mercury is regulated because its methylmercury fraction crosses the placenta and accumulates in developing neural tissue, with no safe threshold established for developmental neurotoxicity

MeHg.name: Methylmercury
MeHg.tox_anchor: methylmercury crosses the blood-brain barrier and the placenta and accumulates in developing neural tissue, with no safe threshold established for developmental neurotoxicity

Ni.name: Nickel
Ni.tox_anchor: nickel carries a chronic tolerable daily intake (EFSA 2020) that the most-exposed young children can exceed, and sensitized individuals react to oral doses well below it

Sn.name: Tin
Sn.tox_anchor: inorganic tin from can linings produces an acute gastrointestinal effect, so its maximum level functions chiefly as a sentinel for can-lining integrity

Al.name: Aluminium
Al.tox_anchor: aluminium accumulates against a low tolerable weekly intake derived from neurotoxic, reproductive, and developmental endpoints, corroborated in humans by dialysis encephalopathy and osteomalacia

Cr-VI.name: Hexavalent chromium
Cr-VI.tox_anchor: hexavalent chromium is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen assessed by US EPA as likely carcinogenic by the oral route, distinct from the low-toxicity trivalent form assumed to dominate in food
